Three cases of progressive multifocal leukoen- cephalopathy (an opportunistic infection of the brain caused by JC virus, a human polyomavirus) have been described in patients given natalizumab.1-3 One patient1 died after receiving natalizu- mab with azathioprine for Crohn’s disease. The other patients2,3 were given natalizumab with interferon beta for multiple sclero- sis; one of these2 also died. After these reports, the use of natali- zumab has been restricted (see Uses and Administration, below). A subsequent retrospective evaluation4 of more than 3000 pa- tients who had received natalizumab found no further cases. However, 2 further cases have subsequently been reported5 in patients taking natalizumab as monotherapy for 14 months and 17 months; one of the patients had previously taken immunosup- pressants. 1.
